 Packers’ Defensive Investments Finally Paying Off
 The emergence of Williams, pass rush offer promise for season’s second half. 
 By Kevin Gibson 
 Nov 06, 2026 
 40 comments 
 It seems like it’s been a long time since it was fun to watch the Green Bay Packers’ play defense. As the 2026 season progresses, however, it’s getting more and more fun.
 If the eye test to a mere fan such as myself isn’t enough of a payoff, I feel like the Packers’ D (G-Fense, if you will) got some validation this week with safety Evan Williams being named NFC Defensive Player of the Month and cornerback Brandon Cisse recognized as NFL Defensive Rookie of October.
 Williams has been increasingly more electric as the season wears on, leading Green Bay’s 10th-ranked defense with 71 total tackles, with the next closest tackler being cornerback Keisean Nixon at 45. Williams also has a pair of interceptions, a sack, two tackles for loss and a fumble recovered, not to mention that he has been frequently used to get pressure on opposing quarterbacks. The kid looks like an All-Pro in the making.
 For his part, the rookie Cisse has tallied 8 passes defensed, 1.5 sacks, an interception and 34 total tackles, and appears to be a player on the rise as well as a second-round steal. 
 For a team that has expended a lot of draft capital on the defensive side of the ball in recent years, it’s a welcome – if belated – payoff. Think about the players still on rookie deals: Williams, Cisse, Javon Bullard, Edgerrin Cooper, Chris McClellan, Barryn Sorrell, Dani Dennis-Sutton – you get the idea.
 Meanwhile, Lukas Van Ness is in the final year of his rookie deal, and Green Bay has already picked up his fifth-year option. Heck, even Ty’Ron Hopper , who had mostly played special teams in his first two-plus seasons, is paying dividends on defense.
 It feels like a culmination of the team’s efforts to develop key players intersecting with the leadership of newly-arrived defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon. Whatever it is, it’s working. And it’s sure as heck fun to watch.
 Gannon’s scheme sans Micah Parsons has looked incredibly confusing for opposing signal callers. On passing downs, there will routinely be seven or eight defenders crowding the line of scrimmage, and at the snap, most usually fall back into coverage. The trouble for quarterbacks and blockers is that it’s nearly impossible to tell on any given down who will rush and who will peel off.
 Often enough, the look just turns into a fairly routine four-man rush. But an opponent can’t bank on that at any given time. And Gannon has brought the blitz on more than 30 percent of snaps.
 With the Packers’ D being as effective as it has been,  it’s led to honors such as those Williams and Cisse received this week. Deserving players are finally getting some recognition outside of Wisconsin.
 "It's definitely a blessing, man, to even be considered for something like that," Williams told the media this week. "I just try to come out every day, put my best foot forward, do the little things right every day, but I feel like it's really more of a group award than anything. We say when we're all succeeding that's when individuals start to see success."
 "He's intelligent… I love how Matt says it, 'if you wanna play like a G, you have to prepare like a G', and he studies and when you study the way he does, he knows what's going on," Gannon said of Willams recently. "Nothing is catching him by surprise… He's playing very well right now." 
 When Parsons returns, we can only hope things will get even more exciting on the defensive side of the ball. 
 And all this is without even mentioning that Packers quarterback Jordan Love is one touchdown pass shy of 100 for his career – fifth in franchise history – and was named the FedEx Air & Ground NFL Player of the Week for Week 8. The offense has certainly given us plenty of memorable moments as well.
 Now, about that running game …
